_README: The beat filter, and the ingestion contract, for the journalist-query lane.
The filter is deliberately strict and rejects freely. docs/EXTERNAL-AUTHORITY-PLAN.md
Rank 1: 'Answer only queries where you have first-hand knowledge -- a 2-in-10
hit rate on 5 good answers beats a 0-in-50 rate on generic ones.' A lane that
surfaces eight plausible queries a day is the same lane that dies in week
three, because it becomes a chore instead of an opportunity.
`keywords` is a cheap prefilter, not the decision. A query that passes it goes
to a second, strict judgement against data/journalist-queries/expertise-ledger.json:
if a grounded answer cannot be built from the ledger, the query is dropped.
`max_per_digest` is a hard cap, not a target. On a day with nothing relevant,
NOTHING IS SENT. Silence on a quiet day is a designed outcome.

beats.label: Memphis events, venues, vendors and wedding cost
Immigration documentation and form or fee changes

_why: A query can match a beat keyword and still be one she must not answer.
These are dropped before the model is asked anything, because the cheapest
way to never send a wrong answer is to never draft one.

_verified: Checked live on 2026-09-01, before any of this was built.
SOURCE OF SOURCES -- email only. sourceofsources.com states: 'Up to three
times a day, you'll get an email filled with queries from journalists across
top media outlets.' The signup form asks for a name and an email address and
nothing else, and the site states 'This list doesn't cost a dime.' There is
no query API. https://sourceofsources.com/feed EXISTS and returns HTTP 200,
but it is the WordPress blog feed (channel title 'Source of Sources',
lastBuildDate Jan 2026, articles like 'How to Create an Online Press Kit').
It is not the queries and must not be used as if it were.
FEATURED.COM -- no public API. https://featured.com/api-integration/sign-up,
named in the plan, returns HTTP 404. https://featured.com/api returns 404.
featured.com/robots.txt disallows /api/. featured.com/questions returns HTTP
429 to automated requests. There is no documented developer surface, so
nothing here is built against Featured; adding it later means adding a new
adapter, not changing this lane's shape.
MAILBOX -- searched the owner's Gmail on 2026-09-01 for mail from
sourceofsources.com, featured.com, helpareporter.com, qwoted.com and
sourcebottle.com in the previous 60 days. Zero messages. She is not
subscribed to any of them yet, so there is currently nothing to ingest and
the lane's honest state is a named stop, not an empty result.
UPDATE 2026-09-02 -- SUBSCRIBED, CONNECTED, AND READING REAL MAIL.
The owner subscribed and set the three IMAP secrets. The lane authenticated
and read a real message on its first run. What it read was the WELCOME email,
not a query digest: 3,914 characters, subject 'Welcome to SOS!'. It refused to
call that a quiet day, which was correct, but it named it UNPARSEABLE_DIGEST,
which was wrong -- a welcome email is not a broken parser. Non-digest messages
are now positively recognised by declared signature.
NO QUERY DIGEST HAS ARRIVED YET. Shankman: 'Your first media query will
arrive within 24 hours, Monday-Friday.' So the field grammar in
query-formats.json remains unproven against a real digest, and says so.
What the publisher states about the format, and what each fact changed here:
'two emails from me per day, usually around 6:30am and another around
1:30pm'  -> the workflow now runs twice a day rather than once.
'typically 10-15 per email, sometimes more'
-> a partial parse is now DETECTABLE and named. A digest that
yields two queries when ten were sent has dropped eight that
nobody knows were there.
'reply directly to the reporter in the email'
-> confirms the reply address is per-query, which the grammar
already treats as a field.

imap.note: The only verified delivery channel is email, so this is the only real adapter. It reads, never sends, and never deletes.
imap._lookback_note: Two days, deliberately more than one run's worth: a missed run must not lose a digest. Safe because queries are deduplicated by identity across runs, so re-reading a digest never re-surfaces a query.

dir.note: A directory of .eml or .txt files. Used by the validator's fixtures, and as an escape hatch if mail is exported rather than read over IMAP.
